question:
What is the output of the following code snippet?

import sys

x = ""
y = ""
print(x is y, sys.getsizeof(x) == sys.getsizeof("a"))
Given the expression `x = 257; y = 257`, under which condition will `x is y` evaluate to True in standard CPython 3.x?
options: It always evaluates to True because 257 is within the global integer cache range.
It evaluates to True only when executed simultaneously within the same code block (e.g., a file or a single line execution cell).
It never evaluates to True because numbers above 256 are always allocated new memory locations.
It evaluates to True only if `sys.setintmaxstrdigits()` is explicitly increased.
answer: It evaluates to True only when executed simultaneously within the same code block (e.g., a file or a single line execution cell).
